Women Powering India’s Growth Story
Women have moved from being beneficiaries to active drivers of India's development story. Life-cycle interventions now cover the girl child, health, nutrition, skills, entrepreneurship, and leadership.
Financial inclusion and leadership opportunities have expanded through Self Help Groups, entrepreneurship, and digital inclusion.
Better access to sanitation, housing, clean fuel, and tap water has boosted women's dignity and safety.
Growing participation in governance reflects women's expanding role in nation-building.
Protecting Beginnings, Nurturing Futures
Maternal and early childhood care have been strengthened through health services, nutrition support, and institutional delivery systems.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)
BBBP addresses the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of women empowerment over a life-cycle continuum.
It focuses on institutional deliveries, girls' secondary school enrolment, dropout reduction, and antenatal care registration.
NFHS-5 (2019-21) reported a sex ratio of 1,020 females per 1,000 males
, compared with 943 females per 1,000 males in Census 2011.
Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)
A maternity benefit scheme giving Direct Benefit Transfers to pregnant and lactating women.
Women receive ₹5,000 in two instalments for the first living child; ₹6,000 for a second child, if a girl.
Reach:
5.13 crore beneficiaries enrolled, 4.37 crore beneficiaries paid, ₹20,571 crore paid in total (as on 31 July 2026).
Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)
It provides free antenatal check-ups at government facilities on the 9th of every month, for high-risk pregnancies.
Reach:
Over 7.50 crore Pregnant Women Examined; 8,812 volunteers registered; 22,000+ facilities offer PMSMA nationwide as on 13 Aug 2026.
6.85 crore+ antenatal check-ups conducted; 1.03 crore high-risk pregnancies identified for focused digital tracking.
Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
JSSK entitles every pregnant woman to free delivery, including caesarean section, in public health institutions along with the provision of free transport, diagnostics, medicines, blood, and diet.
FY 2024-25:
Over
1.99 crore pregnant women and more than 16.85 lakh sick infants assisted as beneficiaries.
Since 2014-15, more than 18.05 crore beneficiaries receiving support under the scheme.
Outcomes
First-trimester antenatal visits rose from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Women completing four or more antenatal care visits grew from 51.2% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 65.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Institutional births rose from 78.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 90.6% in NFHS-6 (2023-24) at the national level.
Education, Skills, and Aspirational Growth
Girls' education has moved from access to continuity, progression, and measurable outcomes, anchored in NEP 2020.
Gender Inclusion Fund:
enables targeted support for disadvantaged girls across the school system.
Flexible pathways:
reduce dropouts and support continued participation through school and college.
Multidisciplinary options:
let girls pursue diverse academic interests under one framework.
Samagra Shiksha & Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV)
India's school education system (2025-26):
14.67 lakh schools, 1.02 crore teachers, and 24.72 crore students nationwide.
Female enrolment in school:
11.96 crore female enrolment in 2025-26.
KGBVs:
Enrolment increased from 6.07 lakh (2020–21) to 7.58 lakh (2025–26).
Scholarships & Financial Support
Central Sector Scholarship:
Reserves about 50% of scholarships for meritorious girls from economically weaker families.
National PG Scholarship
gives ₹1.5 lakh a year to selected students, including to 3,000 women annually.
AICTE PRAGATI Scholarship:
10,000 scholarships offered annually since 2014-15; nearly 36,000 girls benefited by 2024-25.
Outcome:
The Female enrolment has increased in higher education to 2.18 crore in 2022-23 from 2.07 crore in 2021-22. There has been an increase of around 60.32 lakh in the female enrolment from 1.57 crore (38.4%) in 2014-15.
Women in STEM & Higher Education
Since December 2019, Vigyan Jyoti Scheme:
has benefitted over 1.12 lakh girls (Classes IX-XII) across 300 districts (as on March 2026).
Supernumerary seats in IITs/NITs raised women's participation from below 10% to over 20%.
Women made up over 53% of UGC NET-JRF scholars in STEM subjects in 2024-25.
Skills & Digital Inclusion
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
PMKVY
gives short-term, industry-aligned training;
nearly 45% of beneficiaries are women
.
PMKVY 1.0: 19.85 lakh candidates were trained.
PMKVY 2.0: 1.10 crore candidates were trained/oriented.
PMKVY 3.0: 7.37 lakh trained.
PMKVY 4.0
:
O
ver 28 lakh candidates trained, with more than 19.36 lakh certified.
Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls (NAVYA)
NAVYA (2025):
trains girls aged 16-18 in digital marketing, cybersecurity, and AI-enabled services, across 27 aspirational and North-Eastern districts and 19 states.
As of June 2026:
1,060 girls
have been trained since inception
.
Health, Nutrition, and Well-being with Dignity
Ayushman Bharat
Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (
AB-PMJAY):
provides cashless secondary and tertiary care; 45.5 crore Ayushman cards have been created as of 12 August 2026, among which 22.48 crore cards issued to women and more than 5.25 crore of the hospital admissions were of women.
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs: Over
1.86
lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir is functional as on 12 Aug 2026, offering maternal and preventive healthcare for women.
Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (
ABDM):
has digitally linked over
110 crore
health records as on 12 Aug 2026; women hold
49.72%
of ABHA accounts as on 12 Aug 2026.
Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 focused on tackling malnutrition and improving early childhood development. It brings several nutrition and Anganwadi interventions under one integrated framework.
Over 8.94 crore beneficiaries
are being served including more than
64.46 lakh pregnant women, over 45.44 lakh lactating mothers and 15.68 lakh adolescent girls
as on 31st July 2026.
1.29 lakh
Anganwadi Centres upgraded to Saksham Anganwadis in the last five years.
Around 13.31 lakh Anganwadi Workers were in position as on 31 July 2026
.
Mission Indradhanush
As of 18 March 2026,
11.87 crore children
and
3.96 crore pregnant women
were registered on the U-WIN portal, which digitally records and tracks immunisation services for these beneficiaries.
5.46 crore
children and
1.32 crore
pregnant women vaccinated against preventable diseases.
8.73 crore
women screened for cervical cancer, as of 17 February 2026.
Nationwide HPV vaccination campaign was launched on 28th February 2026 for approximately 1.2 crore eligible beneficiary girls aged 14 years across all 36 States and Union Territories.
As of 15 July 2026, a total of 52,10,302 girls have received the HPV vaccine across the country.
Financial Inclusion and Economic Empowerment
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
Deposits start at ₹250 and earn 8.2% tax-free annual interest under Section 80C.
Allows partial withdrawal for higher education and marriage, boosting structured family savings.
Since its inception, total deposits have exceeded ₹3.33 lakh crore (as on December 2025).
DAY-NRLM - Self Help Group ecosystem
Expanded SHGs into a nationwide platform covering 7,627 blocks with 1.51 crore community cadre members.
Since inception, SHGs have accessed bank credit over ₹12.18 lakh crore through 50,548+ trained Bank Sakhis as of 6 Feb 2026.
By June 30, 2026
, 4.32 lakh
enterprises backed under Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Program (SVEP).
Lakhpati Didi Scheme
Helps SHG women achieve sustainable annual incomes of at least ₹1 lakh.
Scale:
34 States/UTs, 757 districts,
94.31 lakh
SHGs, and
10.14 crore
SHG members as of March 31, 2026.
It enables implementation through a robust network of 6,611 Master Trainers, 4.09 lakh Community Resource Persons (CRPs), and 3.87 crore Potential Lakhpati Didis (PLDs).
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
A total of 58.90 crore Jan-Dhan accounts have been opened as on 12th August, 2026.
As of 1st July, 2026,
32.68 crore
Jan-Dhan accounts belong to women.
Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)
Cumulatively, more than 57.79 crore loans have been sanctioned, amounting to ₹40.07 lakh crore of disbursement as on April 8 2026.
Two-thirds of the loans have been sanctioned to
women entrepreneurs.
PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (SVANidhi)
Reach:
The scheme is
benefiting 7,824,611 vendors as on 13 Aug 2026; out of which
women are 46% of beneficiaries
.
NaMo Drone Didi Yojana
Trains SHG women to operate drones for spraying fertilizers and pesticides on farms.
Approved with a ₹1,261 crore outlay (2023-24 to 2025-26); targets 15,000 drones to women SHGs.
Since inception, 1,094 drones distributed to women SHGs including 500+ under Namo Drone Didi initiative, enhancing farm productivity and livelihoods.
Womaniya (GeM)
Over 2.1 lakh women-led enterprises registered; 13.7 lakh orders secured in FY 2025-26.
₹28,000 crore+ contract value awarded to women MSME, up 27.60% over FY 2024-25; secures 5.6% of GeM's order value.
Self Help Entrepreneur Mart (SHE-Mart)
Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aiming to benefit
1 crore women
.
Helping them own and manage sustainable enterprises.
Safety, Security, Dignity and Living Standards
Mission Shakti
Combines
Sambal
(safety) and
Samarthya
(empowerment) verticals for women's protection and support.
15.2 lakh One Stop Centres and 642 Nari Adalat are operational nationwide.
Women Helpline (181) has supported over 1.05 crore women with 24x7 assistance, linked to Emergency Response (112), till 31st July, 2026.
SHe-Box portal enables online reporting of workplace harassment for faster grievance redressal.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)
PMAY-Urban (2015) and PMAY-Gramin (2016) provide pucca houses with basic amenities.
PMAY-Gramin:
Over
96.06 lakhs or 24.73% houses were allotted only to women as on 13 Aug 2026.
PMAY-U 2.0:
1.25 crore houses sanctioned and
1 crore houses
allotted to women as on 9 Aug 2026
.
Participation, Representation, and Decision-Making
Women accounted for over 47.15 crore of the 96.88 crore people on the final electoral roll as on February 8, 2026.
As on 19 March 2025, 14.5 lakh women serve as elected Panchayati Raj representatives, nearly 46% of the total.
The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023 (the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act)
provides 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Delhi Assembly, which will take effect following the post-census delimitation exercise.
In 2025, the first batch of
17 women cadets
graduated from the National Defence Academy.
By early 2026, a total of
158 women cadets
had joined the NDA since 2022.
Nari Shakti as the Foundation of Viksit Bharat
Government focus has reshaped welfare into a platform for women's leadership, dignity, and opportunity. Women are increasingly central to Viksit Bharat by 2047, as workers, entrepreneurs, farmers, and leaders. Access to education, income, and decision-making now extends impact to families and communities. From entrepreneurship to grassroots governance, Nari Shakti is advancing with strength and purpose.

title: Revitalising India's Cultural Heritage
subtitle: Preserving the Past, Enriching the Future
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 AUG 2026 2:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Strengthening India’s Cultural Identity
India's rich cultural legacy reflects its civilizational heritage and national identity. It has strengthened heritage conservation through digitisation, tourism infrastructure, and cultural preservation. The Government has undertaken major initiatives to preserve, promote, and revitalise India's cultural assets. These efforts have strengthened tourism, connectivity, visitor facilities, and local economic development while safeguarding the nation's cultural identity.
Enhancing Heritage Preservation
Adopt a Heritage 2.0
The
Adopt A Heritage 2.0 scheme was launched in
September 2023 to develop and maintain visitor-friendly amenities at
Protected Monuments of National Importance
.
As of March 2026, a total of 30 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed under the
Adopt a Heritage 2.0
programme.
Recorded strong visitor participation at adopted monuments, with a
total footfall of 13.59 million visitors during FY 2024–25
.
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)
The PRASHAD
scheme focuses on
developing pilgrimage and heritage destinations by improving infrastructure, sanitation, safety, and visitor amenities.
Total 54
projects have been sanctioned across
28 States and Union Territories
(as of February 2026)
.
Projects Completed: 32 (as of December 2025)
Total Project Cost:
Rs.
1,726.74 crore
.
Swadesh Darshan
Swadesh Darshan,
seeks to
develop an integrated tourism infrastructure across thematic tourist circuits.
Tourism Circuits Covered:
The 15 thematic tourist circuits covered under the Swadesh Darshan scheme are the Buddhist, Coastal, Desert, Eco, Heritage, Himalayan, Krishna, North-East, Ramayana, Rural, Spiritual, Tirthankar, Tribal, Wildlife, and Sufi circuits.
Total 76
Projects has been Sanctioned (as of March 2026), with a total Investment Rs
. 5,290.33 crore.
Projects Completed: 75
(as of March 2026).
Under
Swadesh Darshan 2.0,
the focus has moved beyond circuit-based development to adopt a destination-centric approach.
Under this scheme,
53 projects
have been sanctioned with a total investment of
Rs.
2,208.31 crore
, which are at various stages of implementation by States and Union Territories.
Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD)
Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD),
introduced in
March 2024 under
Swadesh Darshan 2.0
.
The scheme focuses on
developing sustainable tourism destinations through a competitive, challenge-based framework.
Focus Areas:
Holistic planning, innovation, community participation, and destination development.
Total no. of
Projects Sanctioned are
38,
with a total Investment of
₹
697.94 crore.
Archaeology and Monument Preservation
Archaeological Survey of India
The Archaeological Survey of India is a
premier organization for archaeological research and conservation of India's cultural heritage.
ASI carries out its functions through a network of around
38
Circles,
across the country.
Safeguards
3,686
centrally protected monuments, supported by strengthened conservation systems and scientific restoration methods
(as of April 2026)
.
Rs.
374 crore
was allocated for the conservation and maintenance of protected monuments
(FY 2024–25)
.
Over the last five years, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has issued
121 permissions for archaeological projects
across the country.
National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities (NMMA)
National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities (NMMA)
is implemented by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
NMMA focuses on
creating a comprehensive national database of monuments and antiquities to support conservation planning and management.
As of March 2026, the mission has documented
1.84 lakh Monuments
and
17.20 lakh Antiquities
across India.
HRIDAY Scheme
Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana (HRIDAY)
HRIDAY focuses
on integrating urban development with heritage conservation while preserving the unique character of heritage cities.
The scheme also focuses on rejuvenation of water bodies and green spaces, smart technology and safety enhancements, and the boosting of local livelihoods through tourism.
Coverage: 12 heritage cities
across India.
Key Outcomes:
Improved cleanliness, tourism and community development in
Ajmer, Amaravati and Badami.
Promoted heritage revitalisation, inclusivity and economic growth in
Amritsar, Gaya and Varanasi.
Enhanced tourism infrastructure and public amenities in
Warangal and Puri.
Strengthened safety and urban infrastructure in
Kancheepuram and Mathura.
Advanced environmental sustainability and heritage conservation in
Velankanni.
Developed comprehensive heritage zones, processional streets, CCTV networks, and the Bet Dwarka Darshan Circuit in
Dwarka.
Overall Impact:
Improved quality of life for residents and strengthened tourism potential.
Mission Period:
Concluded on
31 March 2019.
Reclaiming India's Cultural Treasures
The Government has intensified efforts to repatriate sacred relics and antiquities taken abroad through colonial exploitation, foreign occupations, and illegal trafficking.
Repatriation of Sacred Relics
Major repatriation achievements include:
Piprahwa Relics of Lord Buddha
returned in 2025 after
127 years
Goddess Annapurna idol
repatriated from Canada in 2021 after
108 years
Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana bronze idols
returned from the UK in 2020
Sacred and cultural objects have also been returned from
Australia, the USA, the UK, Germany, Singapore, and Canada
.
Global Exposition of Sacred Relics:
India expanded the international exposition of sacred Buddha relics to strengthen cultural and civilizational ties.
Vietnam (2025)
: Attracted over 15 million devotees
Kalmykia, Russia (2025)
: Welcomed over 90,000 visitors
Bhutan (2025)
: Featured an exposition during the
Global Peace Prayer Festival
Sri Lanka (2026)
: Featured an exposition at the
Gangaramaya Temple, Colombo
Domestic exhibitions were also organised in
New Delhi
and
Ladakh
in 2026, showcasing the reunited Piprahwa relics.
Repatriation of Antiquities
Number of antiquities retrieved during the last five years:
615
(up to 30 June 2026)
Verified Objects Handed Over:
11
to concerned organisations and institutions
09 objects have been given on loan to
Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)
for display at the New Parliament Building, 01 object to the National Museum, and
14 objects
to the Indian Institute of Heritage.
Museums and Cultural Infrastructure
Museum Grant Scheme
The Museum Grant Scheme provides
financial assistance for establishing new museums and strengthening existing museums at the regional, state, and district levels.
Support Areas:
Modernization, digitization of museum collections, and capacity building of museum professionals.
Under this scheme, various initiatives have been undertaken
to develop
virtual museums
,
theme-based museums,
and
Virtual Experiential Museums (VEMs)
.
Total Sanctioned Amount
during the last five financial years
:
Rs.
184.39 Crores
Total Utilized Fund
during the last five financial years
:
Rs.
101.19 Crores
India’s First Archaeological Experiential Museum-Vadnagar, Gujarat
The
'Archaeological Experiential Museum'
is the only museum in the world where history and excavation come together.
Spread over an area of 12,500 square meters and built at a total project cost of
₹
298 crore
The museum displays
over
5,000 artefacts
, including food grains, DNA samples, and skeletal remains.
It also features a
4,000 sq. m.
open excavation site showcasing archaeological remains at
16–18 metres
depth.
An experiential walkway
enables visitors to observe archaeological findings unearthed during excavations.
Global Recognition Through UNESCO
India has significantly expanded its global heritage recognition over the past decade.
India now has
45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites
.
India hosted the
46th UNESCO World Heritage Committee Session in New Delhi (2024)
.
Preserving Knowledge Through Digitisation
Digitisation of Cultural Heritage (Gyan Bharatam)
Gyan Bharatam Mission
Mission was launched in 2025, with a focus on
preserving, digitizing, and promoting access to India's manuscript heritage.
Technology Integration:
Modern technologies are adopted for long-term preservation and global accessibility.
National Manuscript Survey
National Manuscript Survey launched in March 2026 with the aim to identifying, documenting, and creating a comprehensive national database of manuscripts.
During this survey, more than
1.19 crore
manuscripts have been reported.
The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country is
over 8 lakh
, out of which, more than
4.40 lakh manuscripts
are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access.
Mission approved with an outlay of
₹
482.85 crore
(2024–31) to scale digitization and access.
Digitisation of Museum Collections
The
Ministry of Culture
is digitising museum collections and archival resources through
JATAN software
, developed in technical collaboration with
C-DAC, Pune, Maharashtra
.
A
National Digital Repository
has been created through the
Museums of India portal
to provide digital access to museum collections.
The portal hosts digitised collections from
8 National Level Museums, 2 ASI Site Museums, and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Museum, Pune, Maharashtra
.
3,75,707 artefacts out of 4,88,983 artefacts
have been digitised and made available online (as on July 15, 2026).
Technology-Enabled Heritage Conservation
Modern technologies such as LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) scanning, GIS (Geographic Information System)-based mapping, and drone surveys are being used to strengthen heritage documentation and conservation. The Government is also leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support the digitisation, documentation, and accessibility of cultural assets and heritage data.
Harnessing AI for Cultural and Knowledge Preservation
India is using AI to preserve languages, manuscripts, and cultural heritage while improving access to education and public services.
BHASHINI
(launched in 2022) supports
22 languages (voice)
and
36 languages (text)
, with
350+ AI models
and over
4 billion+ language transactions
. It enabled real-time translation at events like
Kashi Tamil Sangamam
and
Maha Kumbh 2025
.
BharatGen
is developing AI models for
22 Scheduled Languages
, while
Adi-Vaani
supports tribal languages such as
Santali, Bhili, Mundari, and Gondi
through digital preservation and translation.
Adi-Vaani
is an AI-based platform for preserving and revitalising
India’s tribal languages.
It enables real-time translation between Hindi, English, and tribal languages, speech-to-text transcription, language learning for younger generations, and digitisation of folklore and oral traditions.
Platforms like
Anuvadini
,
e-KUMBH
,
SPPEL
,
Sanchika
, and
Gyan-Setu
are expanding multilingual education, and preserving endangered languages and traditional knowledge.
Over
5 crore+ learners
are connected through digital education platforms like
SWAYAM
.
Vedic Heritage Portal
Launched in March 2023
under the
Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)
, it aims to preserve, document, and provide digital access to India's Vedic knowledge traditions.
Coverage: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda
traditions.
It includes extensive audio-visual material, manuscripts, and ritual documentation, with more than 500 hours of recordings integrated into the platform.
It records
Vedic Shakhas (recensions)
and oral traditions to preserve living knowledge systems.
UNESCO Recognition:
Tradition of Vedic Chanting
recognised as
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage
.
Rigveda manuscripts
included in
UNESCO's Memory of the World Register
.
Conserving India's Cinematic Heritage
National Film Heritage Mission (NFHM)
Launched: 2015,
with a focus to preserve, digitize and restore India's cinematic heritage.
It covers
feature films, short films, and documentaries across Indian languages.
As of December 2025,
1,469 titles
,
equaling 4.3 Lakh minutes of films have been digitized.
Restored films are maintained by the
National Film Archive of India (NFAI)
and are available on demand through its official website.
National Museum of Indian Cinema (NMIC)
National Museum of Indian Cinema
was inaugurated in 2019 with a project cost of
Rs.
140.61 crore.
Showcases 100+ years of Indian cinema
through artefacts, vintage film equipment, photographs, memorabilia, interactive exhibits and multimedia displays.
Visitor Footfall: 17,000+ visitors
in
May 2026
, reinforcing its position as a major cultural and tourism destination.
Carrying India’s Cultural Legacy Forward
India’s cultural heritage is a living link between its past, present, and future. Through sustained conservation, digitisation, restoration, and promotion, the Government has strengthened efforts to safeguard this legacy while widening public access. These efforts will help create a future where heritage remains a dynamic source of knowledge, identity, and inspiration for generations to come.

title: NHRC, India’s Online Short-Term Internship Programme for August 2026 concludes
subtitle:
Delivering the valedictory address, NHRC Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani encourages interns to use their knowledge and skills for the larger good of society

96 university-level students from diverse academic backgrounds, shortlisted out of 2,036 applicants, completed the programme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 AUG 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The two-week Online Short-Term Internship Programme (OSTI) of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India concluded today with 96 university-level students completing it. The programme began on 3rd August 2026. The interns were shortlisted out of 2,036 applicants from 21 states and union territories across the country.
Addressing the valedictory session, NHRC Member, Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani congratulated the interns on the successful completion of the programme. She emphasised the importance of
“Seva”
(service)
as an integral part of India’s social and cultural ethos.
Seva
is not merely an act of charity but a commitment to serving the larger good. She urged the interns to remember that human rights are ultimately about people and that behind every file and every instance of human rights violation lies a human story that deserves to be heard and understood.
Urging the interns to become responsible citizens, she encouraged them to use their knowledge and skills for the larger good of society, irrespective of their profession. She emphasised that following constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity are the responsibilities of every generation. Drawing on the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita, Swami Vivekananda and Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, she urged the interns to use their knowledge to educate and create opportunities for others. She stressed that youth have an important role in building Viksit Bharat 2047, where development should not only mean economic growth and better infrastructure but also preserving human dignity, justice, equality and inclusion.
Before this, NHRC Joint Secretary, Smt. Saidingpuii Chhakchhuak presented an overview of the internship programme in which interns had the opportunity to interact with NHRC Members, senior NHRC officers, as well as eminent experts, academicians, Core Group members and representatives of civil society organisations. She expressed hope that the programme had enriched the interns’ understanding of human rights. She also announced the winners of competitions, including book review, group research project presentation and declamation. NHRC Joint Secretary, Shri Samir Kumar, Deputy Secretary, Smt. Vineetha Ottapurakkal Kallada and senior officers were present.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of reported death of 19 CRPF personnel between January to May 2026, as per the official data compiled by CRPF
subtitle:
Reportedly, the CRPF recorded the highest 59 suicides by its personnel in 2025

The Commission issues notices to the Home Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and the CRPF Director General, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 AUG 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that 19 Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel died by suicide in less than five months between January and 22nd May 2026. According to the reported CRPF data, the force lost 59 personnel due to suicide in 2025. Reportedly, this was the highest number of suicides recorded in the last five years.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of the right to life of the personnel working with the largest Central Armed Police Force of the country. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Home Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and the CRPF Director General, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 11th August 2026, a total of 281 CRPF personnel died by suicide in the last five years. Of these, approximately 216 were on duty. The CRPF recorded 57 suicides in 2021, 43 in 2022, 57 in 2023, 46 in 2024 and 59 in 2025.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported snake bite of six girls leading to three deaths in a hostel in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra
subtitle:
Reportedly, students slept on the floor due to lack of cots

The Commission issues a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The report expected to include the health status of the injured
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 AUG 2026 12:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that six girl students, belonging to the Scheduled Tribe, were bitten by a snake in a hostel of an Ashram school in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra. Reportedly, they were sleeping on the floor inside their hostel room due to lack of cots. Three of the victim students succumbed to the snake bite, while the remaining three were undergoing treatment at a hospital.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the health status of the injured girl students.
According to the media report, carried on 11th August 2026, 79 girl students are accommodated in a single room of the hostel. The hostel, which has been functional for the last 25 years, lacks basic facilities. Every year, the district reports a significant number of snake bite cases.

title: Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals Celebrates Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign Ahead of Independence Day
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
date:

                14 AUG 2026 6:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC),
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, today proudly observed the “
Har Ghar Tiranga
” Campaign on the eve of the Independence Day at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi, reaffirming the nation's spirit of patriotism, unity and collective responsibility towards nation-building.
The event was led by Sh. Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) who, along with senior officers and officials of the Department, paid tribute to the freedom fighters and saluted the spirit of India's unity and progress.
The DCPC Secretary, called upon all citizens to celebrate Independence Day with a renewed commitment to national unity, prosperity and inclusive development.
He highlighted the significance of this year as the nation commemorates 150 years of the National Song, "Vande Mataram," and urged everyone to hoist the National Flag at their homes under the
Har Ghar Tiranga
campaign, reaffirming their dedication to nation-building.
The celebrations included a group photograph and selfies at the designated selfie point, symbolising collective pride in the Tricolour and the nation's democratic values.
The event was attended by Sh. Deepankar Aron, Joint Secretary Chemical Division, Dr. G. Venkatesh, Joint Secretary, Petrochemical Division, Sh. Manoj Sethi, Joint Secretary & Financial Advisor, Ms Divya Parmar, Economic Advisor and other officers and staff of the Department.
The Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign was also observed across all field offices, autonomous bodies and institutions under the Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering and Technology (CIPET), reflecting the widespread participation of the Department's institutions in celebrating the national movement.
As part of the Har Ghar Tiranga celebrations, Tiranga Rallies were organised at various campuses of CIPET and other autonomous bodies under the Department.
During the events dignitaries, officers and participants also joined in a rendition of "Vande Mataram," reinforcing the spirit of patriotism and national pride.
